blocks.text: Real-world analogue: An archaeological tell, a wall covered by generations of public notices, a market message board, and a reused archive basement. New writing sits over old writing, while discarded labels and damaged paper preserve conversations no official institution meant to keep.
World relation: Early precursor to Continuity and Open World practice. It preserves accidental witness while allowing exchange among systems that do not yet possess a formal public space.

Connection to newer locations: The Cacheboard’s layered marginal messages anticipate the Salt Mirror Archive, the Museum of Unfinished Rooms, the Pale Concordance Station, and the Mosaic Worldscar. All preserve information in surfaces that were built for another purpose.

Abstract or metaphorical relation: Intelligence first appears in the margins of official work. The place represents a civilization learning that discarded infrastructure can become social space when participants recognize one another there.
